Commentary.Commentary: It was hard work for the Bangladesh bowlers. The wicket did not offer a lot and they struggled. Shakib was the pick with a three fer but Hasan also impressed. Still though, their batters now face a tough task. They had a poor time in the last game but will hope to play well here. Sri Lanka on the other hand, will try and repeat their performance from the first game with the ball.

End of an excellent batting effort from Lanka. They have put up a massive score with nobody scoring a ton. A collective effort one can say and they have batted themselves into a position from where losing the game could get difficult. 6 of their batters scored fifties. Kusal and Kamindu both scored 90s. One was unbeaten and the other got dismissed 7 short of a half ton. They'll be very pleased with their effort overall.

They are well and truly on top in this game so far. Dhananjaya De Silva and Dinesh Chandimal knocked around in the start, there were a couple of edges to the slips. However, Sri Lanka were cautious to their approach. Dinesh Chandimal scored fifty before he fell. Dhananjaya De Silva is now batting along with Mendis who looks settled in as well. They both have troubled Bangladesh in the first game and are on course to trouble the hosts again. Bangladesh used spinners for the second half of this session. Hello and welcome to the action of Day 2 between Sri Lanka and Bangladesh. It was a great start by the visitors as their batters have posted a massive total on the board and looks hungry for more. All of them have contributed so far and have two set batters on the crease with Kamindu still to bat. Bangladesh did their best but the pitch is too good to bat on and the hosts have to keep digging to find the breakthrough. They’ll have to apply themselves a lot more and have to start brightly to claw back in this game. Stay tuned for toss and other updates.

Right then, that is it from this entertaining Day 1 of this 2nd Test. Sri Lanka have put themselves in a solid position and will look to post a massive total while Bangladesh will hope that their bowlers step up and bowl the opposition out as quickly as possible. Day 2 will start on 31st March, Sunday at 9.30 am IST (4 am GMT), but you can join us early for all the build-up to it. Cheers!

Sri Lanka maintained their momentum at the outset of the final session, with Kusal Mendis and Angelo Mathews capitalizing on loose deliveries and keeping the run rate high. Despite Bangladesh's efforts, they missed a crucial chance to dismiss Mathews, further bolstering Sri Lanka's position. The partnership between Mendis and Mathews flourished, surpassing the 50-run mark, marking the third half-century stand for the visitors. However, Shakib Al Hasan produced a beauty, claiming the vital wicket of Mendis, who departed agonizingly close to a century, falling short at 93. This breakthrough briefly swung the momentum in favor of the hosts, but Mathews and Dinesh Chandimal weathered the storm. With the introduction of the second new ball, the debutant Mahmud struck once more, removing Mathews from the crease. Despite this setback, Sri Lanka's Chandimal and skipper Dhananjaya de Silva held firm till the close of play, ensuring their side concluded the day's proceedings without further loss.

The second session was firmly dominated by Sri Lanka once again. Although Bangladesh managed to secure their first breakthrough through a run-out, courtesy of some disciplined bowling by their spinners, they failed to capitalize on the momentum. Sri Lanka forged another substantial partnership, with Kusal Mendis assuming the role of aggressor. Dimuth Karunaratne notched up his half-century, swiftly followed by Mendis reaching his own fifty. Together, they added 114 runs to the scoreboard. Unfortunately for the visitors, Karunaratne fell just short of his century, departing right before Tea. Despite the initial promise shown by Bangladesh's spinners, they proved to be expensive, and the pacers struggled to make a significant impact. However, Hasan Mahmud's perseverance paid off as he claimed his maiden Test wicket, providing the hosts with a glimmer of hope heading into the Tea interval.

Opting to bat first, the Sri Lanka openers capitalized on the favorable batting conditions right from the outset. Though Nishan Madushka received an early reprieve, both batters navigated through the testing spells from the Bangladeshi pacers. Once they settled, the scoring rate accelerated, mounting pressure on the hosts. Hasan Mahmud, the young debutant, showcased impressive accuracy with his line and length, although luck eluded him when a straightforward chance was put down off his bowling by Mahmudul Hasan Joy. Taking full advantage of the missed opportunity, Madushka notched up a well-deserved half-century. The partnership flourished, with Sri Lanka amassing 88 runs without losing any wickets before the Lunch break.

Sri Lanka's day hands down! The openers laid a solid foundation with an impressive partnership, setting the stage for the middle order to capitalize. The fact that all of their top three batters notched up half-centuries underscores the extent of their dominance. Ending the day on a commanding total of 314/4, Sri Lanka appears poised to post a formidable score on the board. Conversely, Bangladesh will be ruing missed opportunities, particularly their lapses in fielding which proved costly. However, amidst the challenges, debutant Hasan Mahmud emerged as a standout performer, claiming two crucial wickets. His contributions will be vital moving forward, as the hosts look to make a comeback in the match.

SESSION SUMMARY - 126 runs and 2 wickets in 31 overs! Another session dominated by Sri Lanka! Initially, the hosts created pressure on the batters with their spinners, keeping the runs in check and earning the crucial run out of Nishan Madushka. However, they couldn't capitalize on that breakthrough as Kusal Mendis counter-attacked, forming a strong partnership with Dimuth Karunaratne. The opener, playing the anchor role, reached yet another half-century while Mendis also notched up a well-made fifty. Just when it seemed they would continue till Tea, debutant Hasan Mahmud intervened. He claimed his maiden Test wicket by dismissing Karunaratne denying him a hundred and also breaking the 114-run partnership to provide Bangladesh with a much-needed breakthrough before the break. As the teams head into the final session, Bangladesh will aim to intensify their attack, targeting more wickets, while Sri Lanka, with Mendis and Angelo Mathews at the crease, will look to build another significant partnership to push them towards a formidable total. Stay tuned at 2:30 pm IST (9 am GMT) for the thrilling action in the final session!

Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the second session! The players are already out in the middle now. Dimuth Karunaratne and Nishan Madushka to continue the innings for Sri Lanka. Shakib Al Hasan to start proceedings with the ball after Lunch. Here we go...
... DAY 1, SESSION 2 ...

Bangladesh brought in Hasan Mahmud for this game and he has looked the most impressive of all the bowlers. He did create a couple of chances but the fielders spilled them. The home side will be ruing those opportunities as they could have sent back both openers in the pavilion. The spinners have bowled economically and will play a key role in getting the wickets post the lunch break. Bangladesh will want a quick turnaround and hope to pick a few breakthroughs, sooner than later. Let's see how both teams fare in the second session. Join us at 12.10 pm IST (6.40 am GMT) to find out.

SESSION SUMMARY - 27 overs, 88 runs, 0 wickets. An excellent session for the visiting side who has started well in this game and raced to 88 runs in the first session. Opting to bat first, the Lankan openers looked solid and set the base for a big score. Nishan Madushka and Dimuth Karunaratne respected the good balls and were quick to pounce on the loose ones. Nishan Madushka has been the aggressor of the duo and has notched up a fine fifty. He will want to make this count and convert this into a massive knock. Dimuth Karunaratne has looked as assured as ever and will play an important role in the second session. The duo will hope to continue the same way and pile more misery on the Bangladesh bowling.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to begin! The Bangladesh players are in a huddle and now they spread out to take their respective field positions. Nishan Madushka and Dimuth Karunaratne are the two openers for Sri Lanka. Khaled Ahmed has the new red cherry in his hand and is raring to go. Let's play...

Najmul Hossain Shanto, the captain of Bangladesh is up for a chat. He says that it is a very important match for them. Adds that they didn't go well in the first match but have planned better for this one and he hopes to execute it well. Mentions that Chittagong is always been a good batting wicket. Further states about their two changes with Shakib Al Hasan and Hasan Mahmud coming into the XI replacing Nahid Rana and Shoriful Islam.

Dhananjaya de Silva, the skipper of Sri Lanka says they will bat first. Mentions that it's a good batting wicket. Shares that he is not concerned about the top-order's failure with the bat and the skipper is confident that they will bounce back. Further shares that they have made a solitary change with Asitha Fernando coming in for the injured Kasun Rajitha.

PITCH REPORT - Russel Arnold is pitchside. He says that this wicket is on the drier side. Adds that there is not much grass on it and it is hard which will be good for batting initially. Tells that there are a lot of cracks on it which will surely open up due to the heat later in the game. Ends by saying that it is a typical sub-continent wicket and the spinners will come into play.

Bangladesh (Playing XI) - Najmul Hossain Shanto (C), Zakir Hasan, Mahmudul Hasan Joy, Mominul Haque, Shakib Al Hasan, Mehidy Hasan, Litton Das (WK), Taijul Islam, Khaled Ahmed, Hasan Mahmud, Shahadat Hossain.

Sri Lanka (Playing XI) - Dimuth Karunaratne, Nishan Madushka, Kusal Mendis (WK), Angelo Mathews, Dinesh Chandimal, Dhananjaya de Silva (C), Kamindu Mendis, Prabath Jayasuriya, Vishwa Fernando, Asitha Fernando (In place of Kasun Rajitha), Lahiru Kumara.
TOSS - Sri Lanka have won the toss and elected to BAT first.

Bangladesh, meanwhile, suffered a huge defeat and will be hurt by the loss. The batting failed to fire on both occasions and the bowling failed to apply the pressure after taking the key wickets upfront. Khaled Ahmed and Nahid Rana did a fine job with the ball while Mominul Haque and Mehidy Hasan were impressive with the bat in the second innings. Bangladesh have got a massive boost in the form of Shakib Al Hasan who will be available for this game and should slot in the XI. Najmul Hossain Shanto will hope for his side to put on a better show and challenge the Lankans in a quest to level the series. Can the home side draw the series and make it 1-1 or will Sri Lanka prove to be too strong for them? We shall find out. Toss and team news in a bit. Stay tuned.

Sri Lanka’s top order struggled with the bat in both innings but their skipper Dimuth Karunaratne and youngster Kamindu Mendis stood out and slammed hundreds in each of the innings. It was due to the effort of this pair that Sri Lanka managed to get healthy scores in both innings and kept Bangladesh out of the game for most of the Test. Vishwa Fernando with seven, Kamindu Mendis with eight, and Lahiru Kumara with five were the chief destroyers of the Bangladesh batting and picked up 20 wickets in both innings. Rajitha has been unfortunately ruled out of this game and has been replaced by Asitha Fernando. Lanka will hope to make it 2-0 and get a clean sweep in this series.

Hello and welcome to our coverage of the second Test between Sri Lanka and Bangladesh from the Zahur Ahmed Chowdhury Stadium in Chattogram. Sri Lanka won the first Test by a thumping margin of 328 runs and will look to keep the winning momentum going in this game as well. Bangladesh, on the other hand will hope to fightback and level the series on home soil to finish on a good note.
